resale_co.name: Certificate of Compliance for the Resale of One and Two Family Dwellings (CCO)
resale_co.issued_by: City of Northfield Housing Officer (Housing and Zoning)
resale_co.lead_time: Inspections are made within 10 business days of the application. If settlement is 5 days or less from the application, the City does not guarantee an inspection before closing and an extra $10 fee may apply.
requirements: Smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms in good working order, placed by the year the home was built (see fire certificate)
Portable ABC fire extinguisher near the kitchen (packet still lists it; see fire certificate)
Heating certification for every oil or gas fired heating unit, from a NJ licensed plumber or HVAC contractor
Sidewalks, walkways, stairs, driveways and parking areas in good repair
Yard free of weeds; garages, fences and other accessory structures sound
Pools clean; pools, hot tubs and spas over 24 inches deep fenced at least 48 inches high with self-closing, self-latching gates
Exterior wood painted or protected; house number plainly visible from the street
Roof, flashing, gutters and downspouts sound and draining properly
Windows that open can be held open; every habitable room has at least one openable window
Interior in good repair, sanitary, and free of rubbish or garbage
Bathroom window or mechanical exhaust vented outdoors
Heat provided; at least two outlets in each habitable room, a bathroom outlet, a laundry outlet, cover plates on all outlets, GFCI protection within 4 feet of water (if remodeled)
Fences, decks, sheds, pools and similar items built without zoning or construction permits delay the certificate until corrected

fees.label: Resale CCO application and inspection, non-refundable
fees.quote: Non-refundable fee of $85.00 must accompany this application - Checks should be made payable to the City of Northfield

fees.label: Settlement 5 days or less after application (may apply)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Download the 'Application for Certificate of Compliance for Residential Resale (CCO)' packet from the City Forms page, fill in block, lot, settlement date, year built, seller, agent and buyer, and give it to the Housing Officer, City Hall, 1600 Shore Road, Northfield, with the $85.00 non-refundable fee (checks payable to the City of Northfield) and the heating certification for oil or gas heat. Inspections are scheduled for Mondays only by calling 609-641-2832 ext 140 (housing@cityofnorthfield.org). If repairs are still open at closing, the buyer can sign the notarized 'Resale Certification of As-Is Conditions' form; the home cannot be occupied until a re-inspection passes and the Certificate of Compliance is issued.

resale_co.notes: Northfield's Housing Officer runs a resale Certificate of Compliance (CCO) inspection for one and two family homes, based on City Code Chapters 128 and 215 and the 2018 International Property Maintenance Code. The packet linked from the Forms page was last modified July 17, 2026. The City's Uniform Construction Code fee ordinance separately lists a construction code certificate of continued occupancy fee; that is not the Housing Officer's $85 resale inspection, so it is not listed as a resale fee. No Housing Officer name is published on the City site. Rental registration and inspection is a separate program, and short-term rentals of 30 days or less are prohibited in the City. The state smoke certificate fees that were listed under the resale certificate in the earlier check now appear only under the fire certificate.

requirements: Smoke alarms by year built (City packet): before January 1977 battery alarms on each level including the basement and within 10 feet of bedrooms; later homes A/C powered (hardwired), interconnected from August 1984, and from March 1991 A/C powered with battery backup on each level and inside each bedroom

Ten-year sealed battery single station smoke alarms where no alarms exist or when replacing battery alarms; hardwired alarms from original construction or a rehab project may not be replaced with battery alarms
Replace smoke alarms 10 years from manufacture or when they fail tests; replace combination smoke/CO alarms at the end-of-life signal or 10 years
Carbon monoxide alarm within 10 feet of bedroom doors; bedrooms with fuel burning appliances also need a CO alarm

Portable fire extinguisher (form still lists it): minimum 2A-10B:C, no more than 10 pounds, within 10 feet of the kitchen in the path of egress, mounted on the manufacturer's bracket with the top no more than 5 feet above the floor, serviced and tagged by a certified contractor within 12 months or a receipt for a recent purchase, with the owner's manual left for the new occupant

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the NJ DCA Fire Safety service portal ('Start Your Smoke Certification Application'), choosing change of ownership, the closing date and the property location, and pay online. For questions call the Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement at (609) 633-6106. Also ask the City Housing Officer (609-641-2832 ext 140) whether the City's resale CCO inspection is accepted in place of, or in addition to, the state certificate.
authorities.contact_title: Bureau Chief, Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement (listed as the Fire Official in the state fire directory)

evidence.quote: LEAID: 0118-999 Northfield City Fire Prev SMOKE DETECTOR COMPLIANCE Name: Northfield City Bldg Dept

fire_cert.notes: NJ DCA lists Northfield as State enforced (S) and its July 17, 2026 list marks Northfield 'SC' (the State issues smoke certificates), so the DCA online certificate is listed here, with the state fees in N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.9(d) cited from the NJ Register adoption (R.2018 d.074): $45.00, $90.00 and $161.00. However, the state fire directory's Northfield page (survey 5/29/2025) names 'Northfield City Bldg Dept' at 1600 Shore Rd, (609) 641-0601, for smoke detector compliance, and the City's July 2026 resale CCO packet has the Housing Officer check smoke alarms, CO alarms and a fire extinguisher. The City does not say whether its CCO inspection also produces the state smoke certificate. The packet still lists a fire extinguisher, which state law (P.L.2025, c.19) dropped from the sale certificate in February 2025. The directory gives (609) 633-6132 for Louis Kilmer; the Bureau's own page gives (609) 633-6106, which is used here.

other_items.label: Heating certification
other_items.detail: Required for all oil and gas fired heating units, from a NJ licensed plumber or HVAC contractor.

other_items.label: Unpermitted structures
other_items.detail: Any fence, deck, shed, pool or similar item installed without zoning or construction permits delays the Certificate of Compliance until corrected or abated.

other_items.label: Buying as-is
other_items.detail: The buyer can sign a notarized Resale Certification of As-Is Conditions agreeing to make the repairs on the Conditional Certificate of Compliance; no occupancy until a re-inspection passes and the Certificate of Compliance is issued.

open_questions: Does the Housing Officer's resale CCO inspection also issue the smoke/CO certificate, or must the seller also get the NJ DCA online certificate? (DCA marks Northfield 'SC'; the state directory lists the City Building Dept for smoke detector compliance.)
The Housing Officer's name is not published on the City site.
How long the Certificate of Compliance stays valid is not stated.
Does the City still require the fire extinguisher at resale after P.L.2025, c.19?
